name: Script_SqCompiler_Expect
signature: void Script_SqCompiler_Expect(SqCompiler* self, SQObjectPtr* outToken, int expectedToken)

params.self: SQCompiler instance: token at +0, funcstate at +4, lexer state at +0x10, token literal span at +0x28/+0x48
params.outToken: 8-byte SQObjectPtr scratch slot that receives the value of a string/integer/float token (null otherwise)
params.expectedToken: token id the parser requires here: 0x102 IDENTIFIER, 0x103 STRING_LITERAL, 0x104 INTEGER, 0x105 FLOAT, or a plain character such as ']' ',' '=' ')' ':'

summary: The compiler's 'expect this token' primitive: if the current token differs from expectedToken it builds the Squirrel error text "expected '%s'" (token name) or "expected '%c'" (single char) through the inlined Error2 path (sprintf into the 0x100-byte compiler error buffer, then the longjmp/raise helper), then always advances the lexer. The special case (token==0x136 TK_CONSTRUCTOR, expected 0x102 IDENTIFIER) is the grammar's permission to read a constructor as an identifier. The 8-byte outToken slot is filled with the literal object only to keep the compiler's constant pool alive across the Error2 throw path.
evidence: String literals IDENTIFIER/STRING_LITERAL/INTEGER/FLOAT/'expected %s'/'expected %c' in the literal pool at 0x18775C; 0x136==TK_CONSTRUCTOR special case and 0x102==TK_IDENTIFIER follow upstream sqcompiler.cpp Expect(); lexer advance is a call to 0x005FC86C (SQLexer::Lex); Error2 helper 0x001874B4 + 0x005FFA30 (vsprintf); every parser routine (Factor 0x187780, Statement 0x18927C, 0x186CB4, 0x185720) calls it with punctuation/identifier token ids.

name: Script_SqCompiler_Factor

params.self: SQCompiler: token at +0, SQFuncState* at +4, token literal at +0x28 (string len) / +0x48, target-stack vector at +0xC8/+0xD0, scope depth at +0xD4

summary: Primary-expression parser of the Squirrel compiler: dispatches on the current token to local/outer/identifier lookups (with the 'cannot delete a local' / 'invalid constant [%s.%s]' errors), 'this' and 'constructor', numeric/string literals, array '[..]', table '{...}', class, function and lambda literals, unary - ! ~ ++ --, and parenthesised expressions; each alternative leaves one value target on the funcstate target stack. It is the bottom of the precedence chain and also the place where a statement 'expression expected' is produced.
evidence: 4716-byte switch that calls EmitInstruction (0x001BDD50) with _OP_LOAD/LOADINT/LOADBOOL/CLOSURE/GETOUTER/NEG/NOT/BWNOT opcodes and calls the nested function parser 0x00186CB4 and table/array literal builder 0x00187140; pooled strings 'this', 'constructor', 'invalid constant [%s.%s]', 'cannot delete a local', "can't delete an expression", 'expression expected' at 0x7BE695..0x7BE6BF; called only from PrefixedExpr 0x00186150, which is the upstream shape of Factor/PrefixedExpr in Squirrel 2.2 sqcompiler.cpp.

name: Script_SqCompiler_EmitBinaryExp
signature: void Script_SqCompiler_EmitBinaryExp(SqCompiler* self, u8 opcode, void (*subExpr)(SqCompiler*), u32 subExprFlags, u8 operatorByte)

params.opcode: 2.2 opcode to emit: 0x11 ARITH, 0x12 BITW, 0x0F EQ, 0x10 NE, 0x28 CMP, 0x29 EXISTS, 0x2A INSTANCEOF
params.subExpr: parser for the right-hand operand (next precedence level), invoked after the lexer advances
params.subExprFlags: odd flag means subExpr is a member-function pointer offset taken through the compiler's own table
params.operatorByte: operator character/selector stored in SQInstruction._arg3 (+7), e.g. '*' 0x2A, '+' 0x2B, BW_AND 0, CMP_L 3

summary: Shared body of the binary-operator precedence levels: advances the lexer, parses the right operand with the supplied lower-level parser, pops the two value targets from the funcstate target stack (SQFuncState::PopTarget 0x001BE454), pushes the result target (0x001BCE5C) and emits one 8-byte SQInstruction {_arg1=left, op=opcode, _arg0=target, _arg2=right, _arg3=operatorByte} via SQFuncState::AddInstruction (0x001BDD50). The caller supplies only opcode + operator byte, which is why every arithmetic level shares this one function.
evidence: Instruction layout matches Squirrel 2.2 SQInstruction (arg1 word at +0, op at +4, arg0 +5, arg2 +6, arg3 +7) as used by tools/sqbin.py's 2.2 opcode table; opcode constants 0x11 ARITH / 0x12 BITW / 0x28 CMP appear at call sites; funcstate stack helpers 0x001BE454 (PopTarget) and 0x001BCE5C (PushTarget) are visible; five callers are the operator levels 0x188A80, 0x189058, 0x1890A4, 0x189120, 0x186B28.

name: Script_SqCompiler_EqExp
summary: Equality/relational expression level: parses one shift-level expression (PrefixedExpr 0x00186150 and the inlined multiply/add/shift loops) and then folds a chain of ==, !=, <, >, <=, >= operators (and the inlined <<, >>, >>> BITW cases), emitting ARITH/BITW/CMP/EQ/NE instructions through Script_SqCompiler_EmitBinaryExp. Returns as soon as the next token is not a comparison operator.
evidence: Token tests 0x25 '%', 0x2A '*', 0x2F '/', 0x2B '+', 0x2D '-', 0x128/0x129/0x132 shifts (emitting BITW with selector 4/5/6 = BW_SHIFTL/SHIFTR/USHIFTR), then 0x3C '<' (CMP 3), 0x3E '>' (CMP 0), 0x108/0x10A/0x10B (EQ/LE/GE), opcode 0x28 CMP; called by BitwiseAndExp 0x00186904 and BitwiseXor/Or 0x001869C4/0x00185E18, matching the upstream BitwiseOr->Xor->And->EqExp chain.

name: Script_SqCompiler_Compile

params.outClosure: receives the compiled top-level closure object

summary: Top-level compile driver: creates the root SQFuncState named 'main' (0x001BE56C ctor), registers 'this' as local 0 and 'unknown' as the source name, then loops Script_SqCompiler_Statement until end of file or a stray '}', enforcing 'end of statement expected (; or lf)' between statements. It finishes the function with a RETURN instruction (opcode 0x13) and copies the resulting closure into outClosure; on a lexer/compile error it reports through the compiler's longjmp error path.
evidence: Pooled strings 'main', 'this', 'unknown', 'end of statement expected (; or lf)'; calls SQFuncState ctor 0x001BE56C and dtor 0x001BE7AC, Statement 0x0018927C, AddInstruction 0x001BDD50 with op 0x13 RETURN; emits CLOSURE via 0x001BC808 and assigns g_00189054 as the closure's value; only caller is 0x00163254 (the public sq_compile entry).

name: Script_SqCompiler_MulExp
summary: Multiplicative precedence level: parses a prefixed expression (0x00186150) and then loops over '*', '/' and '%' calling Script_SqCompiler_EmitBinaryExp with opcode ARITH and the next-level parser; the loop is the only operator group it accepts, so it is the isolated MultExp of the grammar (the other levels were inlined into their callers).
evidence: Only tokens 0x2A '*', 0x2F '/', 0x25 '%' are tested; opcode 0x11 ARITH; sub-parser pointer taken from the static level table at 0x7354BC (+0x38); no direct callers because it is only referenced from that table (0x001890A0 = 0x7354BC).

name: Script_SqCompiler_PlusExp
summary: Additive precedence level: parses a prefixed expression, then folds the multiplicative group (*, /, %) by delegating to Script_SqCompiler_MulExp through the compiler's static level table, then loops over '+' and '-' emitting ARITH instructions. Equivalent to upstream PlusExp with MultExp inlined at the start.
evidence: Two loops: 0x25/0x2A/0x2F with table entry +0x38 (=0x00186150 PrefixedExpr) followed by 0x2B '+'/0x2D '-' with entry +0x30 (=0x00189058 MulExp); opcode 0x11 ARITH; level table at 0x7354BC.

name: Script_SqCompiler_ShiftExp
summary: Shift precedence level: after the inlined multiply/add levels it loops over '<<', '>>' and '>>>' (tokens 0x128/0x129/0x132) and emits BITW instructions with selectors BW_SHIFTL=4, BW_SHIFTR=5, BW_USHIFTR=6. This is the last level before EqExp in the precedence chain.
evidence: Token 0x128/0x129/0x132 with EmitBinaryExp(0x12 BITW, ..., 4/5/6); sub-level entry +0x28 of table 0x7354BC; the BW selector values match tools/sqbin.py/OPS and upstream sqopcodes.h BW_SHIFTL..BW_USHIFTR.

name: Script_SqCompiler_CommaExp
summary: Comma (sequence) expression: parses one full expression with 0x00185720, then while the token is ',' drops the previous value target from the funcstate stack, advances the lexer and recurses. Used for expression lists that keep only the last value (for-loop increment clauses, parenthesised comma expressions).
evidence: 44-byte body: call 0x00185720 (Expression), loop on token 0x2C ',', call SQFuncState::PopTarget 0x001BE454, Lex 0x005FC86C, self-recursion; called from Statement 0x0018927C, Factor 0x00187780 and the function-statement emitter 0x00187140.

name: Script_SqCompiler_Statement
summary: The compiler's statement parser: one huge switch over all statement keywords - block, local declaration/assignment, expression statement, if/else, while, do/while, for, foreach, switch/case/default, break/continue (with the "'break' has to be in a loop block" checks), return, function declaration, class declaration (synthesising the @INDEX@/@ITERATOR@ metamethods), try/catch/throw and yield. It maintains the SQFuncState stack size/scope depth and emits the corresponding jumps and instructions.
evidence: 10548-byte switch; pooled strings 'end of statement expected (; or lf)', '@INDEX@', '@ITERATOR@', "'break' has to be in a loop block", "'continue' has to be in a loop block", 'cannot create a class in a local with the syntax(class <local>)'; calls Expression 0x00185720, CommaExp 0x00189228, Expect 0x001874EC, AddInstruction 0x001BDD50 and SetInstructionParam 0x001BE384; called from Compile 0x00188C9C and from function bodies 0x00186CB4.

name: maybe_Script_SqValueList_GetItem
signature: int maybe_Script_SqValueList_GetItem(SqValueList* self, u32 unused, int index, SQObjectPtr* out)

params.self: holder object whose list head is at self->[0x1C]->[0x38]; array stride is 8 bytes (SQObjectPtr)
params.out: destination SQObjectPtr, written only when the element is not null

summary: Bounds-free element accessor for a heap array of Squirrel values (8-byte type/value pairs). It compares the element's type word with the tagged null constant 0x01000001 and only copies the value out when the slot is non-null, returning whether it did. Part of the virtual container class whose destructor is 0x0018BF48.
evidence: Compares *(u32*)(...+index*8) with g_01000001 = 0x01000001 (SQOBJECT_CANBEFALSE|_RT_NULL); copy via 0x001BF7D8, which is SQObjectPtr::operator= (tests bit 27 = SQOBJECT_REF_COUNTED and bumps/lowers the shared refcount at +4); listed in the vtable at 0x7589F4 next to the destructor 0x0018BF48 and the clear routine 0x0018BCCC.

name: maybe_Script_SqValueList_Dtor

params.self: container: vptr +0, flags +4 (bit 31 = shutting down), owner/list at +0x14, refcounted block at +0x1C, SQObjectPtr array at +0x2C

summary: Destructor of the Squirrel-value array holder: restores the base vtable, unlinks itself from its owner's child list (0x00245C40 with owner+0x48), releases the refcounted block at +0x1C, resets every 8-byte element to null through the element destructor 0x001BF798 called for each slot (0x00100BE0), then installs the base-class vtable. Any Squirrel value stored here is released exactly once.
evidence: Sets *self = 0x7589F4 (vtable), calls 0x00245C40(self[5]+0x48, self), decrements the refcount at +4 of the object at +0x1C and calls vtable+8 when it hits zero, then 0x00100BE0(self+0x2C, 0x001BF798, 8, count) which invokes a per-element function; 0x001BF798 is SQObjectPtr::~SQObjectPtr (same refcounted test as 0x001BF7D8). Ends by setting the vtable to 0x001E9158 and clearing the owner back-pointer.

name: maybe_Party_CompactSlotTable
signature: void maybe_Party_CompactSlotTable(u8* table, const u32* removeList)

params.table: 20 records of 0x98 bytes; each record's first u16 is an id, +0x88/+0x8C is an 8-byte key
params.removeList: array of slots to clear (values >= 20 ignored)

summary: Compacts a fixed 20-slot record table: clears (memset 0x84 + zero key) every slot listed in removeList, then walks the table in order, and for each surviving record (id != 0 and 8-byte key != 0, kind returned by the Thumb helper 0x100B74 < 7) closes the gap by copying the record down over the first free slot. Keeps insertion order, so the caller sees a dense list afterwards.
evidence: Loop 0..0x13 with index into removeList, record stride 0x98 (r0 = idx*3 + idx<<4, <<3), memset of 0x84 through 0x116AE0, key compare at +0x88; compaction loop calls 0x100B74 (Thumb, returns a record kind, 'cmp r0,#7') and memcpy 0x116C10 of 0x84 bytes; sole caller 0x003BDF58 collects matching entries from a 16-byte-stride vector and passes (*g_003BE008)+0x6B8 as the table.

name: maybe_Ui_List_BuildRowRecord
signature: void maybe_Ui_List_BuildRowRecord(u8* out, const u8* id, u32 mode, u32 flag)

params.out: 0x84-byte display record copied out with memcpy 0x00116C10
params.id: two-byte descriptor (id byte + sub-id byte) that is resolved through the item/character tables
params.mode: 0 selects the 0xE0-offset text table, non-zero the 0x98 one

summary: Builds one 0x84-byte list-row display record: resolves the descriptor through the game tables (0x0063F0AC/0x0063DB5C), looks the id up in a three-entry override table, measures the name/count text with the font-width helpers (0x0051B1FC/0x0011CD80), fills icon/colour/count fields and copies the record to out. Used both by the party status panel and by field gimmick HUD setup, so it is the shared 'name + count + icon' row builder of the 2D UI.
evidence: Calls 0x006F1EEC/0x006F20C0 (game work), 0x00156328, 0x0015141C (16-bit text run), 0x0051B1FC+0x0011CD80 (text width divide), 0x00149814/0x00158F94 (per-character width), 0x0018E934, and ends with memcpy(out,&record,0x84); callers are maybe_Ui_PartyStatusPanel_Build 0x004AC46C, Field_Gimmick3107_SetupDrawObjectFromDesc 0x004B081C and the field scene init 0x004D7B4C.

name: maybe_Ui_ItemList_GetSlotRange
summary: Resolves a record key to a small slot/range id: hashes the first four u16 of the key with 0x005F9650, clamps the result to a byte, and asks the character/item tables 0x0015FA90/0x0015D13C for the first and last index of that id, returning first and storing the width (last-first+1) through the UI text-width helper. Small helper used when a row is built for the party status panel.
evidence: Calls 0x005F9650(&key,4,0) (hash), 0x0015FA90(id), 0x0015D13C(id), 0x0051B1FC(...,0x7FFFFFFF) followed by 0x0011CD80(width) and returns first+extraout_r1 & 0xFF; only caller 0x004AC46C (PartyStatusPanel_Build), which uses the result as a byte field of a status row.

name: maybe_Ui_ItemList_GetSlotCount
summary: Tiny helper that returns the number of usable slots for a mode: picks a base text/graphic table (0x006F1EEC work object + 0xC8 or +0xE8) and writes the constant 100 through the divider helper 0x0011CD80, returning the quotient. Callers use it to size rows/columns of a field or party UI list.
evidence: Two-branch constant table selection then 0x0051B1FC + 0x0011CD80(...,100); no other logic; callers 0x003DDE34, 0x004AC46C, 0x004B081C, 0x004B2CA4, 0x004B2FEC, 0x004D7B4C (status panel / gimmick / scene init).

name: maybe_Party_BuildStatText

params.spec: byte pair at +0/+2 selecting a character and a stat index; +0x2C..+0x4C floats are the stat values

summary: Formats one character-stat line for the status panel: clamps the requested stat index against the character's current level (0x0064005C), interpolates/copies the float table, and then builds the 16-bit text run (0x0015141C) plus colour/size fields for the UI. Returns 1 when the line was produced.
evidence: Reads float members through 0x0011CB38/0x0064005C, compares with the level count at +0x60, calls the text-run builder 0x0015141C and the width helper 0x0051B1FC/0x0011CD80, and is called only from Field_Gimmick3107_SetupDrawObjectFromDesc 0x004B081C and 0x004B2CA4.

name: maybe_Party_BuildStatusPanelData

params.out: receives a 0x44-byte block of 16-bit text runs/colours

summary: Collects the strings and colours for one party/status row: pulls the character name (0x0063F7AC/0x0063EE2C), appends the level/HP/MP figures via the text-width helpers, writes the 0x4A separator and stores the block for the caller. Used by the party status panel builder only.
evidence: Calls 0x006F20C0 (game work), 0x0063F7AC/0x0063EE2C (character record accessors), 0x0051B1FC+0x0011CD80 repeatedly with 3 and 0x4A, 0x00111 3EC and 0x00100A74 (text buffer init), stores into out; sole caller 0x004AC46C.

name: maybe_Party_GetPairSlotId
summary: Maps an unordered pair of small slot indices to a compact id (0x0C..0x15) via a triangular table, so the UI can label a 'compare these two characters/items' row with one number. Falls back to 0x00156F74 for the wildcard case and returns 0xFF when the pair is not representable.
evidence: Switch on first/second with literal returns 0x0C..0x15 forming the triangle (1,2)->0x0C ... (4,5)->0x15; wildcard second==0xFF or first==second delegates to 0x00156F74; only caller 0x0018EC70 (stat text formatter).

name: maybe_Party_RemoveDuplicateIds

params.unwanted: id to drop, 0xFF to only remove duplicates

summary: In-place filter for a six-element byte id list: fills the working buffer, optionally erases every occurrence of one id, then compacts out repeated ids and returns the number of remaining entries. Used when the status screen merges equipment/character ids.
evidence: Two local 6-byte stacks, loop writing 0..5, scan/erase of arg2, then double loop copying *n when != arg2 keeping j behind; callers 0x0018DF1C and 0x0018EC70.

name: maybe_Party_FormatStatValue
signature: u32 maybe_Party_FormatStatValue(u32 kind, int statId, int level, u32 textHandle)

params.level: current level, used to scale the value
params.textHandle: text/allocator handle used to measure the string

summary: Turns one numeric character stat into its display string: selects the per-stat base/scale constants (0x0018EF74/0x0018EF78), applies level scaling with the float helpers, resolves special cases through the id list 0x00149814 and the duplicate filter 0x0018EB44, and measures/writes the 16-bit text run with 0x0051B1FC/0x0011CD80.
evidence: Switch on kind==6, statId-7 < 0x1E, float constants at 0x0018EF74/78, calls 0x00149814, 0x0018EB44 (twice), 0x0018E714, 0x0051B1FC/0x0011CD80; called from 0x0018DF1C and 0x0018EC70 itself.

name: maybe_Gfx_ReleaseTrackedHandles

params.self: table: count at +0x18, 8-byte entries from +0x08 {u32 handle, u32 state}

summary: Walks a list of tracked 32-bit handles and, for every entry whose generation still matches the global registry and whose object exists (0x005F5818 non-null), releases it with reason 3 (0x005F5B94) and marks the slot released. Used as a bulk teardown for graphics/animation handles.
evidence: Loop over self->f_18 with entries at +8, compares entry>>11 with a global generation and indexes a registry with (entry & 0x7FF)*8, checks 0x005F5818 then 0x005F5B94(handle,3) and sets entry+4 = 1; no recorded callers (likely called through a vtable or from an already-named parent).

name: maybe_Fs_IsArcOrTestShader

params.fsHandle: archive/file-system handle passed to the name matcher 0x001009B4

summary: Cheap name filter used while scanning an archive: returns 1 when the current entry is either an '.arc' container or the special 'nw_testshader' entry, otherwise 0. Callers use it to skip/route container entries during a directory walk.
evidence: Two literal comparisons through 0x001009B4 against the pooled strings '.arc' (0x7BF...) and 'nw_testshader'; returns 1 on either match, 0 otherwise; no arithmetic.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_DetachRenderNode

params.self: window: parent object at +0x70, render-node id at +0x98

summary: Detaches the window's render node from its parent: asks the parent object (0x0032570C) to drop the node and, when a node is returned, offsets its draw priority by self->[0x98]<<16 and re-attaches it. Small teardown helper called from the window destructor path.

name: maybe_Ui_Object_CtorWithPriority
summary: Constructor fragment shared by many window classes: allocates/initialises the common UI object with 0x001A66A0, installs the vtable 0x0018FF74 (the g_0018FF74 literal) and sets the default draw priority field at +0x4C to 10. Called from every shop/poker/prize window constructor, so it is the common 'window base with priority 10' initialiser.
evidence: Calls the UI base ctor 0x001A66A0, stores g_0018FF74 at [0], writes 10 to puVar2[0x13] (offset 0x4C); eleven callers are all UI constructors (Ui_ShopWindow_Ctor, Ui_PokerWindow_Ctor, Ui_PrizeWindow_Init, Ui_BigWindow_CtorBase, ...).

name: Ui_Object_DtorSub

params.self: UI object created by 0x0018FF58 (same priority field at +0x4C)

summary: Destructor matching the shared window-base constructor 0x0018FF58: runs the UI base destructor 0x001A6768 (which releases the child ring and returns the block to the UI allocator) and then frees this object with 0x0010F6CC. Every window class that uses 0x0018FF58 has this two-call destructor.

name: Text_CanInsertCellChar

params.self: text page: 24 u16 character cells from +0xEC, layout/width state at +0xFC..+0x118, game work pointer obtained through 0x006F20C0

summary: Gate used before writing a character into a message-page cell: looks the character record up (0x0061BD4C) and rejects it when the glyph is missing; for glyph categories 0..7, 8, 12 and 13 it applies the special 'wide/rare glyph' accounting through the font service (0x006138D4 slot 9) and then checks that the page still has room (used count < limit from 0x0051B1FC(...,100)+1). Only when everything fits does it call Text_InsertLineChar (0x001901F4) to commit the character.
evidence: Reads the cell u16 at self+cell*2+0xEC, calls glyph lookup 0x0061BD4C, compares the glyph category byte against 0xD/8/7/0xC, calls 0x006138D4(work+0x24A98, 9) and 0x0051B1FC(...,100), then tail-calls 0x001901F4 Text_InsertLineChar; sole caller maybe_Ui_EquipRow_ClearEquipMark 0x00618394 shows the same layout is reused by equip rows.

name: maybe_Text_UpdateCellState
signature: u32 maybe_Text_UpdateCellState(TextPage* self, int cell, int mode, int arg4)

params.cell: cell index; 0xFFFF marks an empty cell
params.mode: operation selector 0..n (0 = plain text cell, others compare/insert)

summary: Per-cell state machine for the message/equipment text grid: looks up the glyph record of the cell, takes the global 'compare/owned' checks (0x0066C434/0x0066C5A8/0x0066CCEC) and switches on the requested mode to decide whether the cell may change. It is the guard that Text_InsertLineChar (0x001901F4), the equip-row refresh and the poker/prize windows all call before mutating a cell.

name: Text_RefreshCell
summary: Refreshes one cell after a change: clears/inserts the glyph through 0x00191470 and, when that changed something, re-applies the page font record (Text_ApplyFontRecord 0x0019201C) and re-runs the line layout (0x00191E3C). Returns whether the cell actually changed. Called from the text-buffer move code and from the equipment window input handler.
evidence: 44-byte body: call 0x00191470, on non-zero call 0x00191E3C and 0x0019201C, return bool; callers Text_MoveCharBetweenBuffers 0x002496DC and Ui_EquipmentWindow_HandleInput 0x00617FB0.

name: maybe_Text_CopyLayoutWithOffset

params.self: text page; layout snapshot at +0x1DC (0xEA bytes)

summary: Snapshot helper used by the script command that scrolls a text block: captures the current transform (0x00611228), exports the 0xEA-byte layout block with 0x001913B4, rebuilds it with 0x00190B48, subtracts the block origin from the ten exported 16-bit coordinates and stores the shifted copy back over +0x1DC. Net effect is 'move this text block by the delta of its own origin'.
evidence: Calls 0x00611228 (capture transform), 0x001913B4 (export 0xEA-byte block), 0x00190B48(self,&self->f_1DC,1), subtracts self+0x1DC..+0x1F2 from the exported shorts and memcpy 0x00116C10 back; only caller SQCommand 0x0015179C via the script binding.

name: maybe_Text_Page_SetContent
signature: void maybe_Text_Page_SetContent(TextPage* self, const TextRun* src, int mode)

params.self: text page: 30-cell array at +0x129B, 20-cell array at +0x1273, 0xEA-byte layout at +0x1DC, per-glyph table at +0x48
params.src: source run: 7 u16 pairs at +0x26, extra attributes at +0x96, byte length at +0x1C

This is the 'set the page text' routine used by the script command path.

name: maybe_Text_Page_BuildAtOffset
signature: void maybe_Text_Page_BuildAtOffset(TextPage* self, int offset, const u16* posDelta)
